key_insight: A calibration-aware graph reinforcement-learning router can outperform gate-count-driven routing by choosing hardware SWAP paths that avoid poorly calibrated couplers, improving exact circuit fidelity on IBM Heron r2.
engineering_relevance: For quantum compilers and NISQ hardware operation, this suggests routing should incorporate live calibration data rather than relying only on minimizing SWAP count or two-qubit overhead.
method: Uses a graph reinforcement-learning policy trained with proximal policy optimization (PPO).
Selects SWAPs using same-day IBM Heron r2 calibration data to guide routing decisions.
Evaluated with exact simulated fidelity on nine MQT Bench circuits across three calibration snapshots.
evidence_signal: Pooled mean exact fidelity was 0.727 for the learned router versus 0.440 for SABRE-best20 and 0.481 for target-aware SABRE, with gains concentrated in 5q and 8q circuits.
watch_item: The fidelity gains come with higher routed two-qubit counts and do not generalize uniformly, since all 10q families favored SABRE-best20 under the fixed tree action graph.
paper_title: Graph Reinforcement Learning for Calibration-Aware Quantum Circuit Routing
